claim: Two de novo heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding TRPM3 (V990M and P1090Q) were identified as the cause of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) in eight probands.
source: Recently, two de novo substitutions in TRPM3 (V990M and P1090Q) were identified as the cause of intellectual disability and epilepsy in eight probands with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) (Dyment et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dyment et al., 2019, which is a reference to published scholarly work.

claim: The V990M mutation in TRPM3 results in increased basal intracellular calcium concentrations compared to wild type TRPM3.
source: When performing Fura-2-based calcium imaging on transiently transfected HEK293T cells, we observed significantly higher intracellular Ca2+ concentrations ([Ca2+]i) in cells expressing the two DEE mutants compared to wild type human TRPM3 (WT; GenBank: AJ505026.1), an effect that was much more pronounced in the V990M mutant (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 1A,B showing elevated basal calcium levels in V990M-expressing cells.

claim: The P1090Q mutation in TRPM3 results in increased basal intracellular calcium concentrations compared to wild type TRPM3.
source: When performing Fura-2-based calcium imaging on transiently transfected HEK293T cells, we observed significantly higher intracellular Ca2+ concentrations ([Ca2+]i) in cells expressing the two DEE mutants compared to wild type human TRPM3 (WT; GenBank: AJ505026.1), an effect that was much more pronounced in the V990M mutant (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in Figure 1A,B showing elevated basal calcium levels in P1090Q-expressing cells.

claim: Both V990M and P1090Q mutants are expressed at similar levels as wild type TRPM3.
source: Importantly, both mutants were expressed at similar levels as WT, as assessed based on the fluorescence signal of the C-terminally attached YFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by YFP fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The DEE mutations in TRPM3 lead to increased basal channel activity.
source: These results suggest that the DEE mutations lead to increased basal channel activity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the calcium imaging and current density data showing elevated basal activity in mutant-expressing cells.

claim: Whole-cell currents in response to voltage steps revealed increased current densities in cells expressing the DEE mutants compared to wild type.
source: In line herewith, whole-cell currents in response to voltage steps revealed increased current densities in cells expressing the DEE mutants compared to WT (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pregnenolone sulfate (PS) is an endogenous neurosteroid that activates TRPM3.
source: TRPM3 is a calcium-permeable cation channel that can be activated by heat (Vriens et al., 2011) and by a variety of chemical ligands, including the endogenous neurosteroid pregnenolone sulfate (PS) (Wagner et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wagner et al., 2008 and Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: TRPM3 can be activated by heat.
source: TRPM3 is a calcium-permeable cation channel that can be activated by heat (Vriens et al., 2011) and by a variety of chemical ligands, including the endogenous neurosteroid pregnenolone sulfate (PS) (Wagner et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: TRPM3 is expressed in a large subset of mouse and human somatosensory neurons.
source: TRPM3 is expressed in a large subset of mouse and human somatosensory neurons, where it is involved in the detection of noxious heat and the development of inflammatory pain (Vriens et al., 2011; Vangeel et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2011 and Vangeel et al., 2020.

claim: TRPM3 is involved in the detection of noxious heat and the development of inflammatory pain.
source: TRPM3 is expressed in a large subset of mouse and human somatosensory neurons, where it is involved in the detection of noxious heat and the development of inflammatory pain (Vriens et al., 2011; Vangeel et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2011 and Vangeel et al., 2020.

claim: TRPM3 is expressed in several brain areas, including the choroid plexus, cerebellum, cortex and the hippocampal formation.
source: Moreover, TRPM3 is expressed in several brain areas, including the choroid plexus, cerebellum, cortex and the hippocampal formation (Grimm et al., 2003; Oberwinkler et al., 2005; Zamudio-Bulcock et al., 2011), but its functional role in these areas is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Grimm et al., 2003; Oberwinkler et al., 2005; and Zamudio-Bulcock et al., 2011.

claim: The functional role of TRPM3 in brain areas is unknown.
source: Moreover, TRPM3 is expressed in several brain areas, including the choroid plexus, cerebellum, cortex and the hippocampal formation (Grimm et al., 2003; Oberwinkler et al., 2005; Zamudio-Bulcock et al., 2011), but its functional role in these areas is unknown.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Application of primidone reduced intracellular calcium concentrations in cells expressing wild type or mutant TRPM3.
source: Application of primidone or isosakuranetin, both potent TRPM3 antagonists (Krügel et al., 2017; Straub et al., 2013), reduced [Ca2+]i in cells expressing WT or mutant TRPM3.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Krügel et al., 2017 and Straub et al., 2013.

claim: Application of isosakuranetin reduced intracellular calcium concentrations in cells expressing wild type or mutant TRPM3.
source: Application of primidone or isosakuranetin, both potent TRPM3 antagonists (Krügel et al., 2017; Straub et al., 2013), reduced [Ca2+]i in cells expressing WT or mutant TRPM3.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Krügel et al., 2017 and Straub et al., 2013.

claim: Primidone is a potent TRPM3 antagonist.
source: Application of primidone or isosakuranetin, both potent TRPM3 antagonists (Krügel et al., 2017; Straub et al., 2013), reduced [Ca2+]i in cells expressing WT or mutant TRPM3.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Krügel et al., 2017 and Straub et al., 2013.

claim: Isosakuranetin is a potent TRPM3 antagonist.
source: Application of primidone or isosakuranetin, both potent TRPM3 antagonists (Krügel et al., 2017; Straub et al., 2013), reduced [Ca2+]i in cells expressing WT or mutant TRPM3.

claim: The antagonist-induced reduction in intracellular calcium was largest for the V990M mutant.
source: In absolute terms, the antagonist-induced reduction in [Ca2+]i was the largest for the V990M mutant, yet [Ca2+]i did not fully return to the level of cells expressing WT (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Intracellular calcium did not fully return to wild type levels after antagonist application in V990M mutant cells.
source: In absolute terms, the antagonist-induced reduction in [Ca2+]i was the largest for the V990M mutant, yet [Ca2+]i did not fully return to the level of cells expressing WT (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PS reversibly activated outwardly rectifying whole-cell currents in cells expressing wild type TRPM3.
source: In line with earlier studies (Wagner et al., 2008), we found that PS (40 µM) reversibly activated outwardly rectifying whole-cell currents in cells expressing WT, whereas application of Clt (10 µM) did not activate currents by itself but potentiated responses to PS (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and by citation to Wagner et al., 2008.

claim: Clotrimazole (Clt) did not activate currents by itself in wild type TRPM3 but potentiated responses to PS.
source: In line with earlier studies (Wagner et al., 2008), we found that PS (40 µM) reversibly activated outwardly rectifying whole-cell currents in cells expressing WT, whereas application of Clt (10 µM) did not activate currents by itself but potentiated responses to PS (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2, and by citation to Wagner et al., 2008.

claim: Application of PS in the presence of Clt provoked activation of a large inwardly rectifying current component in wild type TRPM3.
source: In particular, application of PS in the presence of Clt provoked activation of a large inwardly rectifying current component, which has been attributed to activation of an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage-sensing domain, distinct from the central pore (Vriens et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to Vriens et al., 2014.

claim: The inwardly rectifying current component activated by PS and Clt has been attributed to activation of an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage-sensing domain, distinct from the central pore.
source: In particular, application of PS in the presence of Clt provoked activation of a large inwardly rectifying current component, which has been attributed to activation of an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage-sensing domain, distinct from the central pore (Vriens et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Vriens et al., 2014.

claim: Whole-cell current densities in response to PS were significantly larger in V990M compared to wild type TRPM3.
source: In the case of V990M, whole-cell current densities in response to PS were significantly larger compared to WT, and notably, exhibited a prominent inwardly rectifying current component.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental electrophysiological data.

claim: V990M exhibited a prominent inwardly rectifying current component in response to PS.
source: In the case of V990M, whole-cell current densities in response to PS were significantly larger compared to WT, and notably, exhibited a prominent inwardly rectifying current component.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental electrophysiological data.

claim: Application of Clt induced robust currents in the absence of PS in V990M mutant cells.
source: In addition, application of Clt induced robust currents in the absence of PS, whereas currents in the combined presence of Clt and PS were similar in amplitude and shape as WT (Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Currents in the combined presence of Clt and PS were similar in amplitude and shape as wild type in V990M mutant cells.
source: In addition, application of Clt induced robust currents in the absence of PS, whereas currents in the combined presence of Clt and PS were similar in amplitude and shape as WT (Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Whole-cell current densities in response to PS were significantly larger in P1090Q compared to wild type TRPM3.
source: In the case of P1090Q, whole-cell current densities in response to PS were also significantly larger compared to WT, but lacked the inwardly rectifying component observed in the V990M mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental electrophysiological data.

claim: P1090Q lacked the inwardly rectifying component observed in the V990M mutant.
source: In the case of P1090Q, whole-cell current densities in response to PS were also significantly larger compared to WT, but lacked the inwardly rectifying component observed in the V990M mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental electrophysiological data.

claim: Clt did not activate currents in cells expressing P1090Q.
source: Clt did not activate currents in cells expressing P1090Q, and in contrast to WT, inhibited the response to PS (Figure 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Clt inhibited the response to PS in P1090Q mutant cells, in contrast to wild type.
source: Clt did not activate currents in cells expressing P1090Q, and in contrast to WT, inhibited the response to PS (Figure 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both DEE mutants lead to significant changes in channel gating, including increased basal activity and pronounced alterations in ligand responses.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that both DEE mutants lead to significant changes in channel gating, including increased basal activity and pronounced alterations in ligand responses.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data on basal activity and ligand responses.

claim: The concentration-response curve for both mutants was shifted to significantly lower concentrations compared to wild type.
source: We found that the concentration-response curve for both mutants was shifted to significantly lower concentrations compared to WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental dose-response data.

claim: A PS concentration of 10 µM was required to induce a detectable response in cells expressing wild type TRPM3.
source: Notably, whereas a PS concentration of 10 µM was required to induce a detectable response in cells expressing WT TRPM3, we observed robust calcium responses at concentrations as low as 100 nM for V990M and 1 µM for P1090Q.

claim: Robust calcium responses were observed at concentrations as low as 100 nM PS for V990M.
source: Notably, whereas a PS concentration of 10 µM was required to induce a detectable response in cells expressing WT TRPM3, we observed robust calcium responses at concentrations as low as 100 nM for V990M and 1 µM for P1090Q.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental dose-response data.

claim: Robust calcium responses were observed at concentrations as low as 1 µM PS for P1090Q.

claim: The maximal increase in intracellular calcium to saturating PS concentrations was significantly higher in P1090Q expressing cells compared to wild type.

claim: Both DEE mutants show increased responses to the neurosteroid PS.
source: Thus, both DEE mutants show increased responses to the neurosteroid PS.

claim: TRPM3 is a temperature-sensitive channel, activated upon heating.
source: TRPM3 is a temperature-sensitive channel, activated upon heating (Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: The amplitude of the heat-induced response was significantly larger in cells expressing the DEE mutants compared to wild type.
source: Notably, the amplitude of the heat-induced response was significantly larger in cells expressing the DEE mutants compared to WT (Figure 2C,D).

claim: TRPM3 activity is inhibited upon activation of G protein-coupled receptors, via a mechanism that involves direct binding of the Gβγ of trimeric G-proteins to the channel.
source: TRPM3 activity is inhibited upon activation of G protein-coupled receptors, via a mechanism that involves direct binding of the Gβγ of trimeric G-proteins to the channel (Badheka et al., 2017; Dembla et al., 2017; Quallo et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Badheka et al., 2017; Dembla et al., 2017; and Quallo et al., 2017.

claim: In cells expressing wild type or P1090Q, application of 1 µM DAMGO induced a complete and rapidly reversible inhibition of inward and outward currents.
source: In cells expressing WT or P1090Q, application of 1 µM DAMGO induced a complete and rapidly reversible inhibition of inward and outward currents, whereas V990M was only partly inhibited (Figure 2E–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E–I.

claim: V990M was only partly inhibited by 1 µM DAMGO.
source: In cells expressing WT or P1090Q, application of 1 µM DAMGO induced a complete and rapidly reversible inhibition of inward and outward currents, whereas V990M was only partly inhibited (Figure 2E–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E–I.

claim: The DAMGO concentration for half-maximal inhibition of the PS-activated currents shifted from 4.0 ± 0.6 nM for wild type to 40 ± 10 nM for V990M.
source: The DAMGO concentration for half-maximal inhibition of the PS-activated currents shifted from 4.0 ± 0.6 nM for WT to 40 ± 10 nM for V990M (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental dose-response data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: DAMGO was without effect on TRPM3 currents in cells that were not co-transfected with the µ-opioid receptor.
source: Note that DAMGO was without effect on TRPM3 currents in cells that were not co-transfected with the µ-opioid receptor (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Primidone at a concentration of 25 µM caused a full inhibition of PS-activated inward and outward currents mediated by wild type or P1090Q.
source: A difference in sensitivity was also found for the anticonvulsant drug primidone, which at a concentration of 25 µM caused a full inhibition of PS-activated inward and outward currents mediated by WT or P1090Q, but blocked currents mediated by V990M by only ~50% (Figure 2E–G,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E–G,I.

claim: Primidone at a concentration of 25 µM blocked currents mediated by V990M by only ~50%.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E–G,I.

claim: PS-activated currents mediated by wild type or by P1090Q undergo time-dependent desensitization when switching from Ca2+-free extracellular solution to a solution containing 1 mM Ca2+.
source: When switching from the standard, Ca2+-free extracellular solution to a solution containing 1 mM Ca2+, PS-activated currents mediated by WT or by P1090Q undergo time-dependent desensitization (Vriens et al., 2014; Held et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citations to Vriens et al., 2014 and Held et al., 2015.

claim: PS-activated currents mediated by V990M remained stable in the presence of extracellular Ca2+.
source: In contrast, PS-activated currents mediated by V990M remained stable in the presence of extracellular Ca2+, indicating reduced sensitivity to Ca2+-dependent desensitization in this mutant (Figure 2J–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J–M.

claim: V990M shows reduced sensitivity to Ca2+-dependent desensitization.
source: In contrast, PS-activated currents mediated by V990M remained stable in the presence of extracellular Ca2+, indicating reduced sensitivity to Ca2+-dependent desensitization in this mutant (Figure 2J–M).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing stable currents in the presence of Ca2+.

claim: The PS-induced whole-cell currents mediated by V990M showed a prominent inwardly rectifying current component.
source: The PS-induced whole-cell currents mediated by V990M showed a prominent inwardly rectifying current component.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental electrophysiological data.

claim: The inwardly rectifying current component represents ion flux through an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage sensor domain of TRPM3.
source: In earlier work, we have demonstrated that this inwardly rectifying current component represents ion flux through an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage sensor domain of TRPM3, which can be distinguished from the central pore based on its voltage dependence, insensitivity to pore block by La3+ and ion selectivity (including a lower permeability for monomethylammonium (MMA+) compared to Na+) (Vriens et al., 2014; Held et al., 2015; Held et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2014; Held et al., 2015; and Held et al., 2018.

claim: The alternative ion permeation pathway can be distinguished from the central pore based on its voltage dependence, insensitivity to pore block by La3+ and ion selectivity.
source: In earlier work, we have demonstrated that this inwardly rectifying current component represents ion flux through an alternative ion permeation pathway located in the voltage sensor domain of TRPM3, which can be distinguished from the central pore based on its voltage dependence, insensitivity to pore block by La3+ and ion selectivity (including a lower permeability for monomethylammonium (MMA+) compared to Na+) (Vriens et al., 2014; Held et al., 2015; Held et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2014; Held et al., 2015; and Held et al., 2018.

claim: The V990M mutation is located in close vicinity of Asp988 and Gly991.
source: Notably, the V990M mutation is located in close vicinity of Asp988 and Gly991, which we recently identified as critical determinants of the alternative ion permeation pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Held et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural information shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and citation to Held et al., 2018.

claim: Asp988 and Gly991 were identified as critical determinants of the alternative ion permeation pathway.

evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Held et al., 2018.

claim: Gating of the alternative ion permeation pathway is facilitated in V990M, such that it can be activated by PS even when Clt is not co-applied.
source: We therefore hypothesized that gating of the alternative ion permeation pathway is facilitated in V990M, such that it can be activated by PS even when Clt is not co-applied.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural location of the mutation and observed functional changes.

claim: The PS-activated current in the V990M mutant showed a bimodal voltage dependence.
source: We found that the PS-activated current in the V990M mutant showed a bimodal voltage dependence (Figure 3B), its inward current component was resistant to block by the central pore blocker La3+ (Figure 3F,G), and inward currents were reduced when extracellular Na+ was replaced by MMA+ (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The inward current component of V990M was resistant to block by the central pore blocker La3+.
source: We found that the PS-activated current in the V990M mutant showed a bimodal voltage dependence (Figure 3B), its inward current component was resistant to block by the central pore blocker La3+ (Figure 3F,G), and inward currents were reduced when extracellular Na+ was replaced by MMA+ (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: Inward currents in V990M were reduced when extracellular Na+ was replaced by MMA+.
source: We found that the PS-activated current in the V990M mutant showed a bimodal voltage dependence (Figure 3B), its inward current component was resistant to block by the central pore blocker La3+ (Figure 3F,G), and inward currents were reduced when extracellular Na+ was replaced by MMA+ (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The V990M mutation leads to a gain of function at the level of the alternative ion permeation pathway.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that the V990M mutation leads to a gain of function at the level of the alternative ion permeation pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data on voltage dependence, La3+ resistance, and ion selectivity.

claim: All reported DEE patients were heterozygous for the TRPM3 substitutions.
source: Considering that all reported DEE patients were heterozygous for the TRPM3 substitutions (Dyment et al., 2019), and that TRPM3 is functional as a tetramer, it can be expected that patient cells express a mixture of WT and mutant channel subunits, potentially leading to the formation of heteromultimeric channels with variable stoichiometry.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Dyment et al., 2019.

claim: TRPM3 is functional as a tetramer.
source: Considering that all reported DEE patients were heterozygous for the TRPM3 substitutions (Dyment et al., 2019), and that TRPM3 is functional as a tetramer, it can be expected that patient cells express a mixture of WT and mutant channel subunits, potentially leading to the formation of heteromultimeric channels with variable stoichiometry.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TRPM3 channel structure.

claim: Patient cells express a mixture of wild type and mutant channel subunits, potentially leading to the formation of heteromultimeric channels with variable stoichiometry.
source: Considering that all reported DEE patients were heterozygous for the TRPM3 substitutions (Dyment et al., 2019), and that TRPM3 is functional as a tetramer, it can be expected that patient cells express a mixture of WT and mutant channel subunits, potentially leading to the formation of heteromultimeric channels with variable stoichiometry.
evidence: This is inferred from the heterozygous nature of the mutations and the tetrameric structure of TRPM3.

claim: The current densities of PS-induced inward currents in cells expressing a WT:V990M mixture was intermediate between cells expressing only wild type or only V990M.
source: The current densities of PS-induced inward currents in cells expressing a WT:V990M mixture was intermediate between cells expressing only WT or only V990M (Figure 4A,B).

claim: The PS-activated currents in cells expressing a WT:V990M mixture exhibited the typical inwardly rectifying current component.

claim: Clt (10 µM) activated robust currents in cells expressing a WT:V990M mixture.

claim: WT:P1090Q co-transfected cells showed PS-induced current densities that were intermediate between wild type and P1090Q transfected cells.

claim: WT:P1090Q co-transfected cells showed a shift in the rectification pattern of the PS-induced currents that was different from the homozygote situation.

claim: WT:P1090Q cells showed first a potentiation of the PS responses by pre-incubation of Clt, followed by a time-dependent current inhibition.
source: Moreover, the effect of Clt pre-incubation was different in co-transfected cells. WT:P1090Q cells showed first a potentiation of the PS responses by pre-incubation of Clt, followed by a time-dependent current inhibition.

claim: Pre-incubation with Clt blocked PS-induced currents in the P1090Q mutant in isolation.

claim: In the heterozygous condition both DEE mutations lead to a gain of channel function.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that also in the heterozygous condition both DEE mutations lead to a gain of channel function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-transfection experiments showing intermediate phenotypes.

claim: The precise stoichiometry of wild type and mutant subunits in the TRPM3 channels of DEE patients is not known.

claim: Both mutations lead to significant gain-of-channel function, including increased basal activity and higher sensitivity to PS and heat.
source: We here demonstrate that both mutations lead to significant gain-of-channel function, including increased basal activity and higher sensitivity to PS and heat.

claim: V990M exhibits lower sensitivity to block by the anticonvulsant primidone.
